title: Where a power belongs
promptMarkdown: For $a>0$, determine exactly when $f(x)=x^{-a}$ belongs to $L^p(0,1)$ for $1\le p<\infty$, and whether it belongs to $L^\infty$. For $g(x)=x^{-a}$ on $(1,\infty)$, repeat the analysis. Use this to disprove a universal $L^2(\mathbb R)\subset L^1(\mathbb R)$ inclusion.
hintLadder: Integrate the power with cutoffs at both endpoints.
For the counterexample choose $a$ between $1/2$ and $1$.

criteria.criterion: Finds both strict threshold conditions and endpoints.
